Save both full CPU acceptance receipts and substitute their accepted last.pt SHA values. No formal J0/J1/H0/H1 directory may exist.
Review this helper and its SHA; upload only the helper, not current scientific source. Confirm G/code retains the frozen three-repository binding.
Run the stdlib-only precheck on the CPU entry. It does not replace full warmup acceptance or platform release checks.
Reconcile latest allocation-to-release ledger plus remaining hard caps with cumulative 75 GPU hours; this diagnostic adds at most 0.2 GPU hours.
Check live one-H100 availability, default compute mode, and platform policy. Do not enable MPS, change compute mode, or run alongside a warmup.
Replace both SHA placeholders, inspect dry-run, then root decides whether to submit. Formal plan remains four independent GPUs.

workload.validation_selection: same first 512 validation rows in every mode, diagnostic prefix only
workload.restores: fresh deepcopy of accepted architecture warmup plus full RNG before EVERY mode/phase
workload.timing: Each R/T step includes real microbatches construction; frozen evaluate includes validation load/check, catalog, metrics, gzip and summary.
workload.fairness: One active worker in solo; the other three block with CUDA contexts resident. No busy wait or artificial GPU work.
workload.equality: Compare complete initial/final model,alignment,optimizers,scheduler,RNG fingerprints and uncompressed per_sample JSONL records.
workload.measurement_order_limit: Solo precedes concurrent, so CUDA kernels, allocator and host file caches can be warmer later. Report R/T median slowdown for updates 3-20 beside total wall time; no speedup claim from total time alone.
workload.four_card_comparison_limit: Estimated only. Solo means one active worker plus three blocked resident CUDA contexts on the same GPU, not a measurement of four independent GPUs.
